question: In \(\triangle ABC\) with side lengths \(AB=13,\) \(AC=12,\) and \(BC=5,\) let \(O\) and \(I\) denote the circumcenter and incenter, respectively. A circle with center \(M\) is tangent to the legs \(AC\) and \(BC\) and to the circumcircle of \(\triangle ABC.\) What is the area of \(\triangle MOI?\)
solution:
The side lengths form a \(5\)-\(12\)-\(13\) right triangle, so placing its legs on the coordinate axes makes the circle centers easy to describe. Set
\[
C=(0,0),\qquad A=(12,0),\qquad B=(0,5).
\]
The circumcenter is the midpoint of the hypotenuse, giving
\[
O=\left(6,\frac52\right),\qquad R=\frac{13}{2}.
\]
The triangle has area \(30\) and semiperimeter \(15\). Since area equals inradius times semiperimeter, the inradius is \(r=30/15=2\). The incenter is therefore \(I=(2,2)\).

Let \(\rho\) be the radius of the circle centered at \(M\). Tangency to the two leg segments gives \(M=(\rho,\rho)\), with \(0<\rho\le5\). Its contact point \((\rho,0)\) with \(AC\) lies strictly inside the circumcircle. Since \(\rho\le5<R\), the two circles must be internally tangent.

Let \(P\) be their tangency point. Both radii \(MP\) and \(OP\) are perpendicular to the common tangent, so their centers and \(P\) are collinear. Thus
\[
OM=R-\rho=\frac{13}{2}-\rho.
\]
Using the distance formula and squaring gives
\[
\left(\rho-6\right)^2+\left(\rho-\frac52\right)^2
=\left(\frac{13}{2}-\rho\right)^2,
\]
so
\[
2\rho^2-17\rho+\frac{169}{4}
=\rho^2-13\rho+\frac{169}{4},
\qquad \rho(\rho-4)=0.
\]
Because \(\rho>0\), we obtain \(\rho=4\), hence \(M=(4,4)\).

The shoelace formula now gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
[\triangle MOI]
&=\frac12\left|4\cdot\frac52+6\cdot2+2\cdot4
-\left(4\cdot6+\frac52\cdot2+2\cdot4\right)\right|\\
&=\frac12|30-37|=\boxed{\frac72}.
\end{aligned}
\]
The answer is choice \(\text{E}\).
